style: Kalinga Rekha Deula and Pidha Jagamohana, with later limewash and attached Chandi Mandapa
key_structures: Eastern Simhadwara and three other gates
Biraja Rekha Deula, Antarala and six-pillar Pidha Jagamohana
Nabhi Gaya tiled well chamber with metal grille
Bagalamukhi shrine and Ten Mahavidya door panels
Bhushandeshwara and the southwest inscription fragment
special_features: Two-armed Biraja with a trident and a subdued buffalo
Staged survival of displaced carvings in enclosure and temple walls
Five surviving inscriptions documented by the Biraja Mandira Trust
materials: Ceramic tiles and metal grille in the well chamber
period: Earlier sculpture and inscription remains, with the present temple substantially reconstructed in the first half of the nineteenth century
renovation_history: The Temple Trust attributes the present reconstruction to Sudarshan Mohapatra. The enclosing wall and its lintel record are associated with Bhikari Das.
